Thermoelectric effect

Words: 130 Articles: 2
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
A thermoelectric effect couples heat flow and electrical transport. Temperature differences can generate an electromotive force, while electric currents can transport heat. These effects concern nonequilibrium transport and must be distinguished from equilibrium contact potentials.

Seebeck effect

Words: 99 Articles: 1
Thermoelectric effect OurBigBook.com
The Seebeck effect is the generation of a thermoelectric voltage by a temperature difference. Two materials with different thermopowers form a circuit whose electromotive force is the temperature integral of their Seebeck-coefficient difference, with sign set by circuit orientation. In a nondegenerate semiconductor, Electron and hole transport usually give opposite thermopower signs.

Seebeck coefficient (S)

Words: 50
Seebeck effect OurBigBook.com
The Seebeck coefficient is thermoelectric voltage per temperature difference in the small-gradient limit, with its sign depending on the stated voltage and orientation convention. In a two-material loop the net electromotive force is an oriented integral ∫T1​T2​​(S1​−S2​)dT. It is a transport coefficient, so equilibrium density-of-states data alone do not determine it.

Lorenz-gauge reduction of the electromagnetic action

Words: 64
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
The electromagnetic field tensor action differs from the component-gradient potential action by (2μ0​)−1∫∂bAa∂a​Ab​d4x. Integration by parts expresses this term as a boundary integral plus (2μ0​)−1∫(∂a​Aa)2d4x. With the Lorenz gauge and fixed or vanishing boundary data, the two actions therefore differ only by a boundary term. Varying the component-gradient action without restriction gives the potential wave equations; the Lorenz condition must be supplied to recover all Maxwell equations.

Bioelectromagnetism

Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com

Volume conductor

Words: 273 Articles: 4
Bioelectromagnetism OurBigBook.com
A volume conductor is a conducting three-dimensional medium through which electric currents flow. In the quasistatic bioelectric model, the total current density is J=Jp−σ∇u, comprising an impressed source current and its Ohmic return current. Electric charge conservation gives ∇⋅(σ∇u)=∇⋅Jp. An insulating boundary has zero normal total current.

Geselowitz formula (B=Bp−4πμ0​σ​∫S​un′×∣r−r′∣3r−r′​dS′)

Words: 60
Volume conductor OurBigBook.com
For a homogeneous volume conductor with an insulating boundary S, the Geselowitz formula expresses the exterior magnetic field as the primary Biot-Savart law field minus a surface contribution from the induced electric potential. For a current dipole, Bp=μ0​Q×(r−r0​)/(4π∣r−r0​∣3). On a spherical boundary, n′ is parallel to r′, so the surface term has zero radial component at the observation point.

Spherical volume conductor model (∣r∣<a)

Words: 168 Articles: 2
Volume conductor OurBigBook.com
A spherical volume conductor model approximates a conducting body by a sphere, usually with uniform or radially stratified conductivity. It provides explicit forward models for electroencephalography and magnetoencephalography. Its symmetry makes a radial current dipole magnetically silent outside the sphere; departures from spherical symmetry need not retain that property.
Sarvas formula (B=4πμ0​​∇F(Q×r0​)⋅r​)
Words: 127 Articles: 1
Spherical volume conductor model OurBigBook.com
For the exterior of a spherical volume conductor model, put P=∣r−r0​∣, r=∣r∣ and F=rP2+Pr⋅(r−r0​). The displayed Sarvas formula follows by taking the radial component of the Geselowitz formula and integrating the magnetic scalar potential from infinity. It is independent of a spherically symmetric conductivity profile. The sign shown uses B=+μ0​∇U/(4π); conventions defining a magnetic potential with a minus sign reverse U. Sarvas's original paper derives the spherical-conductor field and its consequences for the inverse problem.
Spherical current-dipole logarithmic kernel (ϕ=b1​logr+P−br+P+b​,b=∣r0​∣)
Words: 50
Sarvas formula OurBigBook.com
For r>b and P=∣r−r0​∣, the displayed kernel satisfies ϕ=∫r∞​ds/[s∣sr−r0​∣]. The limit at b=0 is 1/r. Differentiating along Q×r0​, which preserves b, gives (Q×r0​)⋅∇r0​​ϕ=(Q×r0​)⋅r/F. Thus it generates the normalized magnetic scalar potential in the Sarvas formula.

Maxwell–Chern–Simons one-form equation (d∗F+kF=0)

Words: 64
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
For a differential one-form A on an oriented three-dimensional spacetime, varying 21​∫(F∧∗F+kA∧F), with F=dA, gives d∗F+kF=0. With signature (−,+,+), ∗2=−1 on one- and two-forms; writing B=∗F gives dB−k∗B=0 and the identity d∗B=0. An Abelian gauge transformation changes the action by 2k​∫∂M​ΛF. Thus the bulk field equation is invariant, while invariance of the integrated action depends on boundary conditions.

Electromagnetic field (E,B)

Words: 10
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
The combined electric field and magnetic field that determine the Lorentz force on a charged particle.

Electrical circuit

Words: 182 Articles: 6
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
An electrical circuit connects components that carry electric current and sustain electric potential difference differences. Its dynamics may couple electrical resistance, inductance and capacitance.

RLC circuit

Words: 165 Articles: 5
Electrical circuit OurBigBook.com
An RLC circuit combines electrical resistance, inductance and capacitance. Stored energy can oscillate between magnetic and electric forms, while Joule heating dissipates it.

Series RLC circuit

Words: 147 Articles: 4
RLC circuit OurBigBook.com
In a series RLC circuit, the same electric current I=q′ flows through a resistor, inductor and capacitor. Summing their electric potential difference drops gives Lq′′+Rq′+q/C=V, and differentiating gives
LI′′+RI′+I/C=V′.
(1)
The homogeneous damped harmonic oscillator has angular frequency ω0​=1/LC​ and decay rate γ=R/(2L).
Resonant series RLC response (I0​(t)=VM​sin(ω0​t)/R)
Words: 42
Series RLC circuit OurBigBook.com
For a series RLC circuit driven by V(t)=VM​sin(ω0​t) with R>0 and ω02​=1/(LC), substitution shows that I0​=VM​sin(ω0​t)/R solves the current equation. The inductive and capacitive terms cancel at this resonance. Every homogeneous contribution decays, so every solution approaches this periodic response. Its Q factor is Lω0​/R.
Overdamped RLC response
Words: 21
Series RLC circuit OurBigBook.com
When R2>4L/C, the homogeneous series RLC circuit has two distinct negative characteristic roots, [−R±R2−4L/C​]/(2L). Its current is a linear combination of the corresponding decaying exponential functions.
Critically damped RLC response
Words: 23
Series RLC circuit OurBigBook.com
When R2=4L/C, the homogeneous series RLC circuit has one repeated characteristic root, −R/(2L). Its current is e−Rt/(2L)(A+Bt), with constants determined by the initial data.
Underdamped RLC response
Words: 25
Series RLC circuit OurBigBook.com
When R2<4L/C, the homogeneous series RLC circuit response oscillates with angular frequency 1/(LC)−R2/(4L2)​ and envelope e−Rt/(2L). Its characteristic roots form a complex-conjugate pair with negative real part when R>0.

Capacitor

Words: 197 Articles: 4
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
A capacitor stores opposite electric charges on two conductors separated by an insulator. Its capacitance is C=Q/V.

Parallel-plate capacitor (C=ϵA/d)

Words: 64
Capacitor OurBigBook.com
Two parallel conducting plates of area A separated by a small gap d, filled by material of permittivity ϵ, have capacitance C≃ϵA/d when fringing fields are negligible. Indeed, the interior electric field is approximately Q/(ϵA), and the electric potential difference is approximately Qd/(ϵA). A narrow curved capacitor gap has the same leading local approximation when its width is much less than the curvature radius.

Spherical capacitor (C=4πϵ0​ab/(b−a))

Words: 48
Capacitor OurBigBook.com
Two concentric conducting spherical shells of radii a<b with charges Q,−Q have an electric field only in the intervening vacuum: Er​=Q/(4πϵ0​r2) by Gauss's law. Integrating gives a potential difference Q(1/a−1/b)/(4πϵ0​), and hence the displayed capacitance. The electrostatic energy is Q2/(2C), either by charging work or by integrating ϵ0​∣E∣2/2 over the gap.

Capacitor energy (U=Q2/(2C))

Words: 67 Articles: 1
Capacitor OurBigBook.com
A capacitor of capacitance C carrying charge magnitude Q stores
U=2CQ2​=21​CV2=21​QV.
(2)

Fixed-voltage capacitor energy balance (dUfield​=dWmech​+VdQ)

Words: 56
Capacitor energy OurBigBook.com
For a quasistatic change of capacitance at fixed voltage, the capacitor energy is U=CV2/2 and charge is Q=CV. Electrical work supplied to the field is VdQ, so mechanical work is dU−VdQ=−V2dC/2. Increasing the separation of parallel plates makes dC<0: mechanical work is positive even though field energy decreases, because electrical energy returns to the source.

Electromagnetic interaction

Words: 22
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
The electromagnetic interaction is the long-range interaction of electrically charged matter with the electromagnetic field. Its massless gauge boson is the photon.

Electromagnetic radiation

Words: 262 Articles: 7
Electromagnetism OurBigBook.com
Electromagnetic radiation consists of propagating oscillations of the electric field and magnetic field that carry energy and momentum.

X-ray

Words: 43
Electromagnetic radiation OurBigBook.com
X-rays are high-frequency electromagnetic radiation, conventionally with wavelengths of roughly 0.01 to 10nm. The precise wavelength convention varies with context. Hot accreting gas and energetic electronic processes can emit X-rays, whose short wavelengths make them useful probes of compact objects and atomic structure.

Larmor formula (P=6πcq2μ0​a2​)

Words: 82 Articles: 1
Electromagnetic radiation OurBigBook.com
The nonrelativistic radiated power of an accelerated point charge is P=q2μ0​a2/(6πc) in SI units. Integrating its dipole radiation pattern over solid angle gives this result; relativistic motion requires the Lienard generalization.

Liénard radiated-power formula (P=μ0​q2γ6(∣a∣2−∣v×a∣2)/(6π), c=1)

Words: 50
Larmor formula OurBigBook.com
The relativistic generalization of the Larmor formula uses the invariant proper-acceleration magnitude: P=−μ0​q2AaAa​/(6π) in signature (+−−−). In coordinate time this is the displayed expression. For perpendicular magnetic circular motion, γm∣a∣=∣q∣vB, giving P=μ0​q4(γ2−1)B2/(6πm2). The statement concerns total instantaneous emitted power; directional radiation flux is not itself invariant.

Mie scattering

Words: 21
Electromagnetic radiation OurBigBook.com
The electromagnetic scattering solution for a sphere describes the transition between Rayleigh scattering and geometrical optics. Grain-size-dependent efficiencies can produce structure in the radiation-pressure coefficient.

The distance h is measured to the center, so the surface gap is h−R. Relative to the capacitance of an isolated conducting sphere, the enhancement is c(R/h)=C(R,h)/(4πϵR).
The method of images gives a constructive proof. At fixed sphere potential Vs​, start with q0​=4πϵRVs​ at height z0​=h and place its opposite image below the plane. Cancel that image's nonconstant sphere potential by the successive charges
qn+1​=h+zn​R​qn​,zn+1​=h−h+zn​R2​,
(14)
with opposite mirror charges below the plane at every step. The resulting sphere potential is Vs​ and the plane potential is zero. Since qn​=4πϵRVs​sinhα/sinh((n+1)α), summing the sphere charges gives the displayed capacitance. In particular c(y)=1+y/2+O(y2) for small y.
The exact sphere-plane boundary-value problem is also treated in Behunin and colleagues' analysis of sphere-plane electrostatics.

A free Proca field is consistent and has three physical particle polarizations. The difficulty for generic interactions is the ultraviolet behavior of its Proca propagator: the longitudinal numerator makes part of it approach order 1/m2, rather than decay as 1/k2. Longitudinal external polarization vectors also behave as εLμ​=kμ/m+O(m/E). Without suitable identities and cancellations, amplitudes grow with energy and perturbative counterterms of increasing dimension are needed. Conserved-current Abelian models and the Stueckelberg mechanism are important exceptions; a massive interacting vector is not intrinsically inconsistent as an effective field theory.

For a free massive Proca field in the mostly-plus Minkowski metric, the covariant inverse of the quadratic action and the canonical time-ordered product of vector potentials differ locally. With Fourier transform eiq⋅(x−y), the covariant Proca propagator is −i(ηab​+qa​qb​/m2)/(q2+m2−i0), while the literal canonical two-point correlation function subtracts iδa0​δb0​/m2 in momentum space. The time component is nondynamical; its physical-mode numerator is ∣q∣2/m2, rather than −1+(q0)2/m2. The difference is an instantaneous Dirac delta function, not another propagating state. Both expressions agree away from coincidence. This distinction matters when identifying a covariant Green function with a canonical correlator in a constrained field theory.

u=21​(εij​Ei​Ej​+μij​Hi​Hj​),S=E×H,
(97)
and the macroscopic Maxwell equations give ∂t​u+∇⋅S=−E⋅J.

Near and far field

Words: 339 Articles: 9
Electromagnetic wave OurBigBook.com
The near and far field distinguish source-dependent electromagnetic field regions. Close to a localized source, reactive fields and induction terms contribute; sufficiently far away, the leading transverse fields decrease as the inverse distance and carry outgoing power. The radiation zone describes this far-field limit.

Radiation zone

Words: 301 Articles: 8
Near and far field OurBigBook.com
In the radiation zone of a localized source, the leading electromagnetic fields decay as 1/R, are transverse to the observation direction, and satisfy B=R×E/c. Terms decaying faster than 1/R do not contribute to the limiting radiated power.
Intensity of an isotropic radiator
Words: 27
Radiation zone OurBigBook.com
An isotropic source of average power P has intensity
⟨S⟩=4πr2P​
(98)
at distance r. For monochromatic vacuum radiation, its electric-field amplitude is E0​=2⟨S⟩/(ϵ0​c)​.
Multipole radiation
Words: 233 Articles: 6
Radiation zone OurBigBook.com
Multipole radiation expands radiation from localized time-dependent sources into electric and magnetic multipoles. Electric dipole radiation is the leading electric term, while magnetic dipole radiation and higher electric multipoles contribute when the leading term vanishes or higher precision is needed.
Electric dipole radiation
Words: 142 Articles: 3
Multipole radiation OurBigBook.com
For a localized source whose size is small compared with its radiation wavelength, the radiation fields of its electric dipole moment p are
Erad​=4πRμ0​​R×(R×p¨​(t−R/c)),Brad​=c1​R×Erad​.
(99)
Their total instantaneous power is
P=6πcμ0​​∣p¨​(t−R/c)∣2.
(100)
Electric-dipole approximation for radiation
Words: 42
Electric dipole radiation OurBigBook.com
For a source of characteristic size a and angular frequency ω, the electric-dipole approximation requires
cωa​≪1,
(101)
so the source is much smaller than its radiation wavelength. Observing the pure 1/R radiation field additionally requires the radiation zone, R≫c/ω and R≫a.
Angular distribution of electric dipole radiation
Words: 26
Electric dipole radiation OurBigBook.com
If θ is the angle between the observation direction and p¨​, then
dΩdP​=16π2cμ0​​∣p¨​∣2sin2θ.
(102)
Integrating over solid angle uses ∫sin2θdΩ=8π/3 and gives the total electric dipole radiation power.
Radiation damping of a harmonically oscillating charge
Words: 30
Electric dipole radiation OurBigBook.com
A charge q undergoing simple harmonic motion of angular frequency ω and slowly varying amplitude A radiates the averaged power
⟨P⟩=12πcμ0​q2A2ω4​.
(103)
Its mechanical energy E=mA2ω2/2 therefore has exponential decay rate γ=μ0​q2ω2/(6πmc) and half-life
t1/2​=μ0​q2ω26πmclog2​.
(104)

Multipole radiation OurBigBook.com
Electromagnetic duality replaces the electric dipole p by m/c for a magnetic dipole moment m. Therefore
P=6πc3μ0​​∣m¨∣2.
(105)
This is the magnetic-dipole term of the multipole radiation expansion.

Ω˙=−IC​Ω3,Ω(t)−2=Ω0−2​+I2C​t.
